setup.pitch: Low on food and one day from the nearest village, the party reaches Briar Hollow just as a badly scratched hunter returns carrying a massive owlbear egg. Three villagers argue over whether to eat it, raise it, or return it. Before they can decide, the enraged father owlbear tears into the village.
setup.gmSummary: The adventure has one spine: force the hungry party into Briar Hollow, reveal the stolen owlbear egg, let three NPCs argue three solutions, interrupt the debate with the father owlbear attack, expose the fake druid, then branch only when the party decides the egg's fate. If the party feeds the father their last rations, he leaves and they go hungry. If they kill him, the carcass proves feverish and unsafe to eat; the mother answers from the ridge and later enters a barbarian-like rage. If they refuse to intervene, the father destroys Briar Hollow. Eat the egg and the mother attacks at dawn. Keep the egg and it hatches and imprints on a present PC/NPC, but the mother still comes for her surviving offspring. Return it or leave it at the village edge and the mother retrieves it. If the father survived, the family withdraws peacefully; if he was killed, the mother secures the hatchling and attacks in Maternal Rage.
setup.background: The party has only its final day of trail food left when the road points toward Briar Hollow, itself nearly out of food. Torren Vale, the village hunter, failed to find game and instead stole a huge owlbear egg from a nest. One parent raked his face as he escaped. Mara Dell wants to cook it. Torren, shaken by what he did, wants to raise the hatchling and make the theft mean something. Elmorrow Reed presents himself as a druid and argues that he should return the egg to nature, but he is actually an animal broker for the Moonpetal Traveling Menagerie. The father follows Torren's scent and the egg into town. He is gaunt, feverish, and starving; hunger has overwhelmed his normal protective behavior, which is why food can interrupt the attack.

quest.objective: Survive the owlbear family's response to the stolen egg and decide what Briar Hollow will do with it.
quest.stakes: The party's remaining food, the survival of Briar Hollow, a living owlbear family, and the party's responsibility for whichever solution they choose.
quest.deadline: DAWN: the egg hatches. Show the shell worsening after every major scene: knock → hairline crack → spreading crack → hatch.
successConditions: The party responds to the father owlbear attack.
The party learns enough to understand Elmorrow's real motive or knowingly accepts the risk of trusting him.
The party makes a deliberate choice about the egg and resolves the resulting consequence.
failureConditions: The party knowingly refuses to intervene while the father destroys Briar Hollow.
The party abandons the egg decision after the village has paid the price for the theft.

facts.text: Briar Hollow is nearly out of food, just like the party.
Torren stole the owlbear egg from a nest; the long scratch across his face came from one of its parents.
Mara wants to eat the egg, Torren wants to raise it, and Elmorrow claims he wants to return it.
Elmorrow is not a druid. He intends to sell the live egg or hatchling to the Moonpetal Traveling Menagerie.
The father owlbear will stop the attack and leave if given the party's remaining rations.
Killing the father provokes an answering scream from his mate on the ridge.
The mother enters a barbarian-like maternal rage if the egg is destroyed/stolen from her or if her mate is killed; a true return can calm the family if the father still lives.
If the party keeps the egg, the hatchling imprints on a random present player character or named NPC.
Returning the egg peacefully only works cleanly if the father survived. If the party killed him, the mother may recover the hatchling but still attacks in grief and rage.
The father is starving and feverish. If killed, his carcass is unsafe to eat and cannot solve the village's food shortage.

secrets.text: Elmorrow's wagon contains a signed acquisition contract for one live juvenile owlbear, a collapsible beast crate, and sedatives.
secrets.revealCondition: Solve or force the wagon strongbox, inspect the crate hardware, or catch Elmorrow trying to leave with the egg.

npcs.name: Mayor Sella Vane
npcs.role: mayor and referee of the egg debate
voiceCues: asks what each choice costs tomorrow
wants: Stop the argument from turning into a riot
Force someone to accept responsibility for the egg
fears: The village losing its remaining food
knows: The village is nearly out of food
Torren brought the egg back moments ago
cannotKnow: Elmorrow's real employer until evidence appears

revealRules.fact: The village cannot spare the party replacement rations.
revealRules.when: The party asks what happens if they feed their food to the father.

npcs.questFunction: Keeps the scene moving and forces the final choice without endorsing one.
npcs.description: A lean, sleepless woman in a patched wool coat, with ink on her fingers and a ration ledger tucked under one arm.
tableDialogue: “If there were a good answer, we'd have found it before you got here.”
“Tell me what this choice costs tomorrow, not what it lets us feel tonight.”
“Choose it, then own it. That's all I can ask.”

reactions.agreement: Nods once and immediately asks who is carrying out the decision.
reactions.refusal: Does not argue; asks what alternative keeps the village alive.
reactions.accusation: Meets it without flinching and opens the ration ledger.
reactions.danger: Moves civilians first and gives short, practical orders.

npcs.name: Torren Vale
npcs.role: hunter who stole the egg; advocates raising it
voiceCues: touches the scratch on his face when challenged
stops pretending the theft was smart once pressed
wants: Raise the hatchling rather than waste the theft
Avoid admitting fear drove him home with it
fears: The parent owlbears finding the village
knows: He stole the egg directly from a nest
One adult caught him and raked his face
The nest lies on the ridge
believes: If they already paid for the egg in blood, killing it now makes the theft pointless
secrets: He expected the egg to feed the village at first, then changed his mind after feeling it move
lies: Initially says he 'found' the egg until confronted about the scratch

revealRules.fact: Torren stole the egg from an active nest.
revealRules.when: Anyone asks directly about the scratch or succeeds on Insight DC 10.

npcs.questFunction: Embodies the raise-it option and supplies the theft reveal.
npcs.description: A soot-stained hunter with a bandaged claw wound across his face, cut rope at his belt, and hands that will not stop shaking.
tableDialogue: “I thought it was food until I felt it move.”
“I stole it. I know what that makes me.”
“If we crack it now, then all I brought home was another corpse.”

reactions.agreement: Relief breaks through the shame; he volunteers to guard or carry the egg.
reactions.refusal: Argues once, then goes quiet and stares at the shell.
reactions.accusation: Touches the scratch and admits the theft if pressed.
reactions.danger: Freezes for a beat, then tries to pull people away from the owlbear.

npcs.name: Mara Dell
wants: Prevent a dangerous predator from hatching in town
knows: The village stores are almost gone
The egg is large enough for one major communal meal
believes: A stolen predator egg is food when people are starving
cannotKnow: What the mother will do at dawn

revealRules.fact: Cooking the egg feeds everyone once but does not solve the shortage.
revealRules.when: Anyone asks what the meal actually buys.

npcs.questFunction: Embodies the eat-it option without being cruel.
npcs.description: A broad-shouldered baker in a flour-white apron, with oven burns on both forearms and a cleaver resting flat beside the dough board.
tableDialogue: “You can't feed a village with ideals.”
“One proper meal. Tomorrow we're hungry again. I know that.”
“Warm shell or not, I've got children chewing bark.”

reactions.agreement: Immediately starts planning portions, broth, and who eats first.
reactions.refusal: Accepts it with a hard look but demands a real replacement plan.
reactions.accusation: Does not defend herself morally; points toward the empty bins.
reactions.danger: Gets children and noncombatants into the bakehouse or out the rear lane.

npcs.name: Elmorrow Reed
npcs.role: fake druid and Moonpetal Traveling Menagerie beast broker
wants: Convince the village to hand him the egg
fears: Being exposed before he gets custody
knows: The egg is close to hatching
Sedatives and reinforced crates can transport dangerous animals
believes: Hungry villagers will accept a clean-sounding solution
secrets: His wagon is prepared to transport the hatchling
He has a purchase contract from Moonpetal Traveling Menagerie
lies: Claims he will return the egg to its nest
Claims a druid circle sent him
cannotKnow: Who the hatchling will imprint on

revealRules.when: Nature DC 12 catches shallow lore or his wagon evidence is found.

revealRules.fact: He intends to sell the owlbear.
revealRules.when: The strongbox contract or Moonpetal crate stamp is found.

npcs.questFunction: Presents the apparently noble return-it option while secretly turning the owlbear into merchandise.
npcs.description: A clean-bearded traveler in a moss-colored cloak, carrying a polished staff and speaking with the calm patience of someone rehearsing a role.
tableDialogue: “The kindest thing is to return it to the wild.”
“Give it to me. I know where creatures like this belong.”
When exposed: “A cage is safer than a grave.”

reactions.agreement: Moves quickly to take custody and get the wagon moving.
reactions.refusal: Applies gentle pressure, calling delay dangerous and selfish.
reactions.accusation: Deflects with nature language until hard evidence appears.
reactions.danger: Protects himself and the wagon first; flees rather than fighting to the death.

locations.name: Road to Briar Hollow
locations.description: A muddy two-rut road between thorn scrub and pine, exposed to cold wind and distant war sounds; Briar Hollow lies one hungry day east.

locations.name: Briar Hollow Square
locations.description: A roughly 60-foot village square boxed by a half-empty granary, low bakehouse, timber stable, well, and muddy lanes. Smoke and thin stew hang in the air; when danger starts, the stable wall and granary become obvious breakable terrain and the west/south lanes are the cleanest escape routes.

locations.name: Mara's Bakehouse
locations.description: A low, flour-dusted room warmed by a brick oven, crowded with worktables, sacks, blankets, hooks, and the smell of yeast. The egg dominates the central table; the rear door opens to a narrow lane while the front door faces the square.

locations.name: Elmorrow's Green Wagon
locations.description: A polished green healer's wagon that smells of mint, leather, and bitter sedatives. Beneath the tarp are a collapsible iron beast crate, reinforced straps, a Moonpetal stamp, and a puzzle-locked strongbox; the driver's bench points toward the fastest road out of town.

locations.name: Edge of Briar Hollow
locations.description: A low stone wall and wet open field separating Briar Hollow from the dark ridge woods. The treeline begins 30–40 feet beyond the wall, giving the party clear sight lines, poor cover in the field, and two obvious retreat paths back toward the square.

scenes.title: One Day From Food
scenes.purpose: Get the hungry party to Briar Hollow without creating an adventure branch before the adventure starts.
scenes.readAloud: The road has narrowed to two muddy wheel-ruts between scrub pine and thorn, and the last crumbs in your packs smell more like leather than food. Ahead, a warped sign leans east beneath a circling crow: BRIAR HOLLOW — ONE DAY; west is longer, and the northern forest track disappears under black branches. Somewhere far off, axes or drums carry on the wind. Whatever road you choose, hunger is coming with you.
gmNotes: The party has exactly one day of travel rations left between them for the purpose of this adventure.
If they choose Briar Hollow, move on immediately.
If they choose any other route, use the orc warband to close that path. This is a boundary threat, not the adventure's first tactical fight.
Telegraph overwhelming numbers before damage. If they retreat, they reach Briar Hollow. If they knowingly insist on a suicidal stand after the warning, a TPK is possible.

runSteps.title: Read the boxed text
runSteps.text: Establish that food is nearly gone and Briar Hollow is the nearest settlement.

runSteps.title: Ask where they go
runSteps.text: If they choose Briar Hollow, advance. If not, bring the orc warband onto the alternate road.

runSteps.title: Push, do not detour
runSteps.text: Make the warband obviously overwhelming and drive retreat toward Briar Hollow. Do not spend the session on this threat.

exitChoices.label: Enter Briar Hollow
exitChoices.description: The village is nearly as hungry as the party.

scenes.title: The Hunter Comes Home
scenes.purpose: Reveal the stolen egg and put the three competing solutions in front of the players before the father interrupts.
scenes.readAloud: Briar Hollow smells of woodsmoke, damp wool, and a stew thin enough that you can see the bottom of the communal pot. The granary doors stand open on bins scraped nearly bare when Torren Vale staggers into the square with an egg almost as large as his chest and a fresh claw-mark from temple to jaw. “I found food,” he pants, while Mara the baker stares at the shell and Elmorrow Reed folds his moss-green cloak around himself like a priest at a funeral. The egg knocks once from the inside.
gmNotes: Torren first says he found the egg. Anyone who asks about the scratch or succeeds on Insight DC 10 gets the truth: he stole it from an owlbear nest.
Three positions: Mara says eat it. Torren says raise it. Elmorrow says let him return it to nature.
Elmorrow should initially sound like the cleanest moral answer.
Sella moderates. She is not a fourth option.
Do not resolve the debate. The father attack interrupts it.
VISIBLE CLOCK 1/4: the egg knocks once from inside. Put 'HATCHES AT DAWN' in front of the players.

runSteps.title: Read the boxed text
runSteps.text: Show the village's hunger, Torren's scratch, and the giant living egg.

runSteps.title: Reveal the theft
runSteps.text: Questioning Torren or Insight DC 10 gets the admission: he stole the egg from an active owlbear nest.

runSteps.title: Present exactly three options
runSteps.text: Mara: eat it. Torren: raise it. Elmorrow: he will return it.

runSteps.title: Let players argue briefly
runSteps.text: Give each NPC one strong argument. Keep Elmorrow credible.

runSteps.title: Interrupt with violence
runSteps.text: Before a final decision, the father owlbear crashes into the village.

scenes.advanceWhen: The three options are understood and the father attack interrupts the debate.

exitChoices.label: The father crashes into the village
exitChoices.description: Run the feed, fight, or do-nothing consequence.

scenes.title: The Father Tears Through Briar Hollow
scenes.purpose: Force a real choice: sacrifice the party's food, fight a starving feverish parent, or allow Briar Hollow to be destroyed.
scenes.readAloud: The argument ends when the stable wall bursts outward in a spray of splinters, straw, and frightened horses. A gaunt owlbear crashes into the square—mud-black feathers, ribs showing through its hide, foam stringing from its beak—and two villagers with boar spears rush it before anyone can stop them. One spear snaps; one villager hits the mud; the other disappears beneath beak and claws. Then the creature freezes, lifts its bloody head, and turns toward the smell of your remaining food.
gmNotes: If the party does nothing, the father kills the spear villagers, smashes the granary and bakehouse, and destroys Briar Hollow. Take the village-destroyed branch.
If the party throws its remaining rations, the father immediately stops attacking, devours them, and leaves. The party goes without food; the village cannot replace the rations.

If the party kills the father, inspection makes the payoff explicit: he is feverish and diseased. Mara/Pell confirms the carcass is unsafe to eat, so killing him does not solve the food shortage. Immediately answer with the mother's scream from the ridge.
Creative solutions are allowed, but resolve them back into one of three states: father leaves alive, father dies, or village is destroyed.
Do not apply starvation exhaustion immediately just because the party skipped one meal; use normal food-deprivation rules if time extends beyond this adventure.
VISIBLE CLOCK 2/4: when this scene ends, show a hairline crack in the shell whether the father lived or died.

runSteps.title: Read the boxed text
runSteps.text: Make the villagers' failed spear charge demonstrate that ignoring the father has consequences.

runSteps.title: Ask what the players do
runSteps.text: The core choices are give up the last rations, fight, or stand aside.

runSteps.title: If they feed him
runSteps.text: No check. He eats all remaining party rations and leaves the village. The party will be hungry.

runSteps.title: If they fight
runSteps.text: Run the father stat block. If he dies, immediately reveal the sick carcass is unsafe food, then play the mother's scream from the ridge.

runSteps.title: If they do nothing
runSteps.text: Do not soft-pedal it. He destroys the village; advance to the failure resolution.

scenes.advanceWhen: The father leaves, dies, or destroys Briar Hollow.

exitChoices.label: The party intervened
exitChoices.description: The village survives. Continue with the egg and Elmorrow.

exitChoices.label: The party does nothing
exitChoices.description: The father destroys Briar Hollow. Resolve the failure ending.

scenes.title: The Druid Is Too Ready to Leave
scenes.purpose: Expose Elmorrow before the egg decision without creating a separate investigative branch.
scenes.readAloud: Briar Hollow now smells of blood, wet feathers, smoke, and spilled grain, and the villagers move through the square in stunned silence. Elmorrow Reed is not helping the wounded; he is hitching his green wagon, where something beneath the tarp gives a heavy metallic rattle. “We have seen what comes of keeping this creature here,” he says, too smoothly. “Give me the egg. I can return it before the mother comes.”
gmNotes: Point the party at the wagon. Do not require them to invent the investigation.
The strongbox puzzle is player-facing. Correct order: EGG → CHAIN → TENT → COIN.
Inside is the Moonpetal Traveling Menagerie contract for one live juvenile owlbear, sedatives, and a handler token.
If the party skips the puzzle, the crate stamp or Elmorrow's attempt to flee reveals enough truth. The fake druid twist must not be missable.
If trusted despite evidence, Elmorrow can take the egg; treat that as the keep/lose-responsibility variant, not a fourth main moral option.
VISIBLE CLOCK 3/4: while Elmorrow stalls, the crack branches and the egg rocks. The players can see they do not have all night.

runSteps.title: Read the boxed text
runSteps.text: Make Elmorrow's urgency and hidden cage obvious enough to investigate.

runSteps.title: Run the strongbox puzzle
runSteps.text: EGG → CHAIN → TENT → COIN. Let the players solve it before offering rolls.

runSteps.title: Use fail-forward if needed
runSteps.text: Thieves' tools DC 13 or Strength DC 14 opens it. Failure still exposes the crate stamp/contract.

runSteps.title: Reveal the lie
runSteps.text: Elmorrow is not returning the owlbear; he intends to sell it to the Moonpetal Traveling Menagerie.

runSteps.title: Return to the real choice
runSteps.text: Now the party decides the egg's fate without a false clean option.

scenes.advanceWhen: The party understands Elmorrow's real motive.

exitChoices.label: Decide the egg's fate
exitChoices.description: Eat it, keep it, or return/leave it for the mother.

scenes.title: Three Choices, No Clean Answer
scenes.purpose: Branch the adventure only now, when the players actually choose what happens to the egg.
scenes.readAloud: Mara's bakehouse is the warmest room in Briar Hollow, but nobody seems comfortable inside it. The egg rests on the flour-dusted worktable, warm enough to fog the cold air, its shell webbed with fresh cracks while Mara stands beside a cleaver, Torren touches the bandage on his face, and Sella watches all of you instead of the egg. From beyond the shuttered windows comes a deep owlbear call from the ridge. The shell moves again.
gmNotes: VISIBLE CLOCK 4/4: the egg is hatching now. The party must choose what to do with it before dawn resolves the choice.
There are three core choices now. Do not add another branch unless the players genuinely invent one.
EAT: Mara cooks the egg. The village and party get a full meal. At dawn, the mother attacks.

KEEP: the egg hatches and imprints on a present PC or named NPC. The mother still comes for the hatchling; the final consequence depends on the father's fate and whether the party yields or keeps the baby.
RETURN / LEAVE AT EDGE: the mother retrieves the egg. Father alive = family withdraws peacefully. Father dead = she secures the hatchling, then attacks in Maternal Rage.
Elmorrow may still bargain or flee, but he no longer controls the structure.

runSteps.title: Read the boxed text
runSteps.text: Bring the table back to the egg and make it clear hatching is close.

runSteps.title: Restate the three actual options
runSteps.text: Eat it. Keep/raise it. Return it or leave it for the mother.

runSteps.title: Let the players choose
runSteps.text: Do not steer them toward a preferred answer.

runSteps.title: Take the matching branch
runSteps.text: Each option has its own consequence scene. Do not resolve the ending here.

scenes.advanceWhen: The party commits to one egg choice.

exitChoices.label: Eat the egg
exitChoices.description: The village eats tonight. The mother comes at dawn.

exitChoices.label: Keep and raise the egg
exitChoices.description: The egg hatches and chooses someone.

exitChoices.label: Return it / leave it at the edge
exitChoices.description: The mother retrieves it, it hatches, and the village faces the consequence.

scenes.title: Dawn Comes Angry
scenes.purpose: Resolve the eat-the-egg branch with the promised mother owlbear fight.
scenes.readAloud: For the first time in days, Briar Hollow smells like real food: hot fat, browned bread, herbs, and steam rising from bowls held in shaking hands. The meal fills every stomach in the square, but at dawn every dog begins barking toward the ridge at once. A huge mother owlbear steps from the mist, scarred shoulders rolling beneath wet feathers, and the square goes silent when she lowers her head to the pile of broken shell. Her scream rattles shutters.
gmNotes: Run the mother in Maternal Rage from the start.
If the father was killed, describe her rage as even more personal, but do not stack a second mechanical rage.
Maternal Rage: advantage on Strength checks/saves, +2 Strength-based melee damage, and resistance to all damage except psychic for 1 minute.
This is the cost of the eat branch: they got the food, and now they must survive the mother.

runSteps.title: Read the boxed text
runSteps.text: Pay off the meal, then reveal the mother at dawn.

runSteps.title: Start the mother already raging
runSteps.text: Use the quick combat block. Make her visibly fixate on shell fragments and the people around them.

runSteps.title: Resolve the boss fight
runSteps.text: Survive, drive her away, or evacuate the village.

runSteps.title: Close on the cost
runSteps.text: They chose food and saved people from hunger for a night, but the choice brought this fight.

scenes.advanceWhen: The mother is driven off, defeated, or the survivors escape.

scenes.title: The Baby Chooses — Then Mother Arrives
scenes.purpose: Resolve the keep branch as both an emotional imprint and a real decision about standing between a mother and her surviving offspring.
scenes.readAloud: After midnight the egg splits with a wet crack, spilling shell and warm fluid across Mara's blankets. A beak pushes free, then two oversized paws, and the hatchling tumbles into the room, blinking through damp feathers before fixing on one person and stumbling toward them with a hungry chirrup. Its first clumsy step is answered by a booming call from the ridge. The hatchling goes still and answers.
gmNotes: Determine the imprint first. The hatchling bonds behaviorally to a present PC/NPC; it is not magical domination.
The mother does NOT disappear from this ending. She comes for her surviving offspring before dawn.
If the father survived, the mother approaches cautiously rather than raging. The party may surrender the hatchling and get a peaceful family withdrawal.
If the party actively keeps the hatchling from her, she escalates to violence after clear warnings/posturing.
If the father died, the mother arrives already primed for Maternal Rage. Returning the hatchling may still let her secure the baby, but she remains hostile toward the killers/village.
The imprint creates emotional friction: the hatchling cries and follows its bonded protector, but instinctively responds to the mother's calls too.
The party can choose: surrender the hatchling, retreat and let the family reunite, evacuate with the hatchling, or fight to keep it. Do not dictate which is morally correct.

runSteps.title: Hatch and imprint
runSteps.text: Build the present-character list and determine the bonded protector.

runSteps.title: Bring in the mother
runSteps.text: Her call comes from the ridge almost immediately; she is searching for her surviving offspring.

runSteps.title: Check the father's state
runSteps.text: Father alive: mother starts cautious. Father dead: mother is grief-stricken and much more likely to rage.

runSteps.title: Ask what the party actually does
runSteps.text: Yield the hatchling, back away and let the family reunite, flee/evacuate with it, or deliberately keep it.

runSteps.title: Resolve the consequence
runSteps.text: Yielding with father alive can end peacefully. Deliberately keeping the hatchling can trigger the mother fight. Father dead keeps the mother's hostility in play even if she recovers the baby.

scenes.advanceWhen: The hatchling's long-term custody is decided and the mother's response is resolved.

scenes.title: The Mother Comes for Her Egg
scenes.purpose: Resolve the return/edge branch according to the father's fate: peaceful family recovery if he lived, enraged assault if the party killed him.
scenes.readAloud: The field beyond Briar Hollow is silver with dew, and the low stone wall behind you feels much too small when the mother appears between the ridge trees. She circles the egg once, smelling shell, grass, and every footprint around it before drawing it beneath one massive forelimb. The shell cracks open under her chest and a damp, oversized head pushes into the cold air. From the ridge, another owlbear call answers only if the father still lives.
gmNotes: If the father survived: this is the cleanest return. The mother gathers the hatchling, the father answers from the ridge, and the family withdraws. No combat.
If the father was killed: the mother recognizes his scent on the party/village, enters Maternal Rage, and attacks after securing the hatchling behind her.

If the father's fate is ambiguous because of a creative solution, classify it honestly: father alive = peaceful return; father dead = rage; father driven away but alive = peaceful withdrawal after tense posturing.
Do not punish a genuine successful return with combat unless the party previously killed the father.

runSteps.title: Read the boxed text
runSteps.text: Let the players see the mother recover the egg and the hatchling emerge.

runSteps.title: Check the father's state
runSteps.text: Father alive: the family withdraws. Father dead: the mother recognizes the loss and rages.

runSteps.title: If father lived
runSteps.text: End without combat. Describe both adults calling to the hatchling from the ridge as the family disappears into the trees.

runSteps.title: If father died
runSteps.text: Run the mother in Maternal Rage. Evacuation remains a valid resolution.

runSteps.title: Close on consequence
runSteps.text: The ending reflects the party's earlier choice: mercy makes peaceful return possible; killing the father carries forward.

scenes.advanceWhen: The owlbear family withdraws peacefully, or the enraged mother is driven off/defeated and the village survives or evacuates.

scenes.title: Briar Hollow Falls
scenes.purpose: Honor the do-nothing choice with a clear failure resolution instead of pretending the adventure continues normally.
scenes.readAloud: Nobody stops it. The father tears through the square, then the granary, then Mara's bakehouse, while smoke, flour, splintered wood, and frightened screams turn Briar Hollow into a choking blur. Those who can run scatter into the fields; those who cannot are left behind. When the owlbear finally disappears into the dark, there is no village left to save—only burning roofs, broken grain bins, and bodies in the mud.
gmNotes: This is a real failure ending. Do not quietly reset the village so the egg debate can continue.
Survivors blame Torren for the theft and the party for standing aside.
If desired, the egg may be gone with the father or buried in the ruins, but the one-shot is over.

runSteps.title: Read the boxed text
runSteps.text: State the consequence plainly.

runSteps.title: Resolve survivors
runSteps.text: Let the players help the wounded or leave, but do not reopen the main adventure.

runSteps.title: End the one-shot
runSteps.text: The choice not to act was itself the ending.

scenes.advanceWhen: The table accepts the destruction of Briar Hollow as the consequence.

clues.revelation: Briar Hollow is nearly out of food and cannot replace the party's rations.
sources: physical evidence: empty grain bins and thin communal stew
Sella says the village has no spare travel food
Mara shows the last flour and beans

clues.revelation: Torren stole the egg from an active owlbear nest.
sources: physical evidence: fresh talon scratch across Torren's face and egg-nest debris on his coat
Torren admits the theft when confronted
the father tracks Torren and the egg directly into the village

clues.revelation: Elmorrow is a beast broker, not a druid, and intends to sell the owlbear.
sources: physical evidence: Moonpetal Traveling Menagerie acquisition contract
physical evidence: reinforced beast crate stamped with the Moonpetal mark
Nature DC 12 exposes his rehearsed but shallow druid lore

clues.revelation: The mother owlbear is alive on the ridge and becomes violently enraged by the family's loss.
sources: if the father dies, her scream answers immediately
huge tracks appear at the village edge before dawn
Torren remembers a second, larger shape at the nest

clues.revelation: The mother reacts differently depending on whether her mate survived: returning the egg can end peacefully if the father lives, but not if the party killed him.
sources: physical evidence: paired adult tracks converge on the ridge trail when the father survives
Torren recalls that two adults guarded the nest together
if the father dies, the mother's answering scream makes the loss unmistakable

clues.revelation: The father is feverish and his carcass is unsafe to eat.
sources: physical evidence: foam at the beak, inflamed gums, foul-smelling lesions under the feathers
Medicine DC 10 identifies systemic sickness before or after death
Mara or Pell inspects the carcass after the fight and refuses to butcher it

encounters.name: Orc Warband on the Road
encounters.summary: If the party refuses Briar Hollow, an orc raiding column closes the alternate road and drives them toward the village.
encounters.resolution: Reach Briar Hollow. This encounter exists to close the map, not to consume the session.
encounters.special: Clearly telegraph overwhelming numbers. If players insist on a suicidal stand after warning, the warband can kill them.

encounters.name: Ragged Father Owlbear
encounters.difficulty: Low by XP (700 XP); high consequence if ignored
encounters.summary: The starving, feverish father tracks the stolen egg into town and tears through anyone between him, food, and the egg.
encounters.resolution: Feed him the party's remaining rations, kill him, drive him off creatively, or refuse to intervene.
encounters.talkOut: He cannot be reasoned with, but food overrides his rage.
encounters.bypass: Throw the party's remaining rations into the square. He devours them and leaves.
encounters.special: Ragged Exhaustion gives Disadvantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws. If the party does nothing, two spear-bearing villagers are killed immediately and the father destroys Briar Hollow. If killed, his feverish carcass is unsafe to eat and the mother's scream answers from the ridge.

encounters.name: Enraged Mother Owlbear
encounters.summary: At dawn the mother arrives enraged over the destroyed or missing egg.
encounters.resolution: Survive, drive her off, or escape the village.
encounters.talkOut: No normal social check ends the rage once combat begins.
encounters.bypass: Only available before combat by abandoning the village and egg.
encounters.special: Maternal Rage: Advantage on Strength checks/saves, +2 Strength-melee damage, and resistance to all damage except psychic for 1 minute.

encounters.name: Mother and Hatchling — Only if Father Died
encounters.summary: On the return branch, this combat occurs only if the father was killed. If he survived, the mother retrieves the hatchling and the family leaves.
encounters.resolution: Father alive: no combat. Father dead: drive the mother away, survive until she withdraws, or evacuate the village.
encounters.talkOut: Father alive: no check is needed; the return succeeds. Father dead: once Maternal Rage begins, normal social checks do not end it.
encounters.bypass: Keep distance and allow the family to withdraw if the father survived; evacuate rather than defend if he died.
encounters.special: The hatchling uses the half-grown profile. If the mother rages, she gains Advantage on Strength checks/saves, +2 Strength-melee damage, and resistance to all damage except psychic.

encounters.name: Mother Comes for the Kept Hatchling
encounters.difficulty: social/tense if father alive; deadly if the party refuses or father died
encounters.summary: The mother comes for the hatchling after it imprints. The confrontation depends on the father's fate and whether the party yields the baby.
encounters.resolution: Yield the hatchling, back away and allow reunion, evacuate with the hatchling, or fight to keep it.
encounters.talkOut: Father alive: no roll is needed if the party visibly yields and backs away. Father dead: social checks cannot erase grief, but surrendering the hatchling may keep her focus on recovery rather than pursuit.
encounters.bypass: Do not stand between mother and hatchling; retreat and let the family reunite.
encounters.special: Father alive + visible surrender can end without combat. If violence starts, the mother can enter Maternal Rage: Advantage on Strength checks/saves, +2 Strength-melee damage, resistance to all damage except psychic.

puzzles.name: Shell Before Shackle
puzzles.prompt: Elmorrow's brass strongbox has four sliding picture tiles: an EGG, a CHAIN, a CIRCUS TENT, and a SILVER COIN. Scratched below them: “Shell before shackle, shackle before show; show before silver — that's how fortunes grow.” Put the tiles in order.
puzzles.failForward: Thieves' tools DC 13 or Strength DC 14 opens the box. Failure brings Elmorrow running, but his crate stamp and exposed contract still reveal the truth.

items.name: Stolen Owlbear Egg
items.description: A massive living egg stolen from an active owlbear nest.

items.name: Party's Last Rations
items.description: The party's final day of food. Feeding all of it to the father ends his attack immediately.

playMaps.title: Briar Hollow Square — 60×60 ft.
playMaps.caption: Village square battle map. Use for the father attack, dawn mother assault, or a KEEP-branch confrontation if the party refuses to yield the hatchling.

playMaps.title: Briar Hollow Edge — 80×60 ft.
playMaps.caption: Village edge and ridge field for the returned-egg assault.
notes: Low stone wall across west side
Egg starts 35 ft outside the wall
Evacuation routes lead south and west

events.name: The Mate Answers
events.effect: If the father dies, the mother screams from the ridge immediately.

events.name: The Baby Chooses
events.effect: On the keep branch, roll randomly among all present PCs and named NPCs unless the party deliberately isolated one caretaker.

endings.name: Eat the Egg
endings.result: The village gets a real meal. At dawn the mother attacks in Maternal Rage.

endings.name: Keep and Raise It
endings.result: The egg hatches and imprints on a present PC/NPC. The mother then comes for her offspring: father alive allows a peaceful reunion if the party yields; keeping the hatchling can provoke combat. If the father died, the mother's grief keeps the ending dangerous even if she recovers the baby.

endings.name: Return It / Leave It at the Edge
endings.condition: The party returns the egg or leaves it for the mother.
endings.result: If the father survived, the mother retrieves the hatching egg and the family leaves peacefully. If the father was killed, she secures the hatchling and attacks in Maternal Rage.

endings.name: Briar Hollow Destroyed
endings.condition: The party refuses to intervene against the father.
endings.result: The father destroys the village and the one-shot ends as a failure.

recovery.principle: Keep the adventure on one spine. Move information forward instead of opening side branches.
policies: If the party misses a clue, deliver it in the next unavoidable scene.
Do not create a second investigation path before the father attack.
Only branch when the party's action creates a different consequence.

routes.trigger: The party refuses to go to Briar Hollow
routes.response: The orc warband closes the alternate route and drives them toward Briar Hollow.

routes.trigger: The party never confronts Torren about the scratch
routes.response: The father's arrival proves an adult owlbear tracked him and the egg; Torren blurts out the theft during the attack.

routes.trigger: The party refuses to inspect Elmorrow's wagon
routes.response: His beast crate stamp and acquisition papers fall into view as he tries to load the egg. The fake-druid truth is still exposed before the final choice.

routes.trigger: The party resolves the father with an unexpected plan
routes.response: Classify the result as father alive/leaves, father dead, or village destroyed, then continue from that state.

routes.trigger: The party invents a fourth egg solution
routes.response: Allow it only if it clearly pays a cost equivalent to one of the three core branches; otherwise ask what happens to the egg by dawn.

pathPressure.principle: The adventure stays on one spine until a real consequence branch. The ending is never locked by a missed check; the players still finish the one-shot, but their choices can produce different terminal outcomes.

prepared.when: They expose Elmorrow before choosing the egg
prepared.payoff: They make the final decision without being manipulated by the fake druid.

prepared.when: They preserve their rations by killing the father
prepared.payoff: They keep their food but provoke the mother's rage.

rushed.cost: They save the village without bloodshed but spend their last food and go hungry.

rushed.when: They do nothing during the father attack
rushed.cost: Briar Hollow is destroyed and the one-shot ends in failure.

notDeviation: Eating the egg is not failure.
Keeping the egg is not automatically kind.
Returning the egg is not automatically safe.
The fake druid is a lie, not a fourth moral answer.

oneshotRecipe.shape: linear consequence chain with one final three-way branch
oneshotRecipe.tale: A hungry party reaches a hungry village just as a stolen owlbear egg brings its family to the door.

rooms.note: Branch only here; each choice pays off.

cutOrder: If 30+ minutes behind, resolve Elmorrow's strongbox with the crate stamp immediately after one failed attempt.
If 20+ minutes behind at the final choice, summarize NPC arguments in one sentence each and ask for the decision.
Never cut the father consequence, sick-meat payoff, or the mother's response to the final egg choice.
optionalOrder: Extra NPC debate after each advocate has made one strong argument.
Extended bargaining with Elmorrow after his lie is proven.
Detailed survivor roleplay after a terminal ending.

notes: Use the SRD-style owlbear quick-run block supplied in this package. Feeding the pooled rations is an authored encounter resolution, not a spell or class feature.
Use the same encounter numbers for this adventure unless the table prefers a current SRD owlbear stat block. The authored feed-or-fight resolution is unchanged.

checks.label: Read Torren's story
checks.success: His story about 'finding' the egg collapses; he admits he stole it from an active nest.
checks.failure: The father attack later proves the theft and Torren admits it then.

checks.label: Test Elmorrow's druid lore
checks.success: His nature language is rehearsed and shallow; he is not trained as a druid.
checks.failure: The wagon evidence still proves the lie.

checks.label: Force or pick the strongbox if the puzzle is not solved
checks.success: The box opens on the Moonpetal contract, handler token, and sedatives.
checks.failure: Elmorrow arrives, but the crate stamp and exposed paperwork still reveal his purpose.

encounters.objective: Close the alternate road and push the party toward Briar Hollow.
encounters.start: An orc raiding column appears in overwhelming numbers on the route away from the village.

creatures.name: Orc Raiders
creatures.trait: Overwhelming Column: reinforcements continue arriving; this is not balanced as a stand-up fight.
creatures.tactics: Advance in numbers, cut off the road, and force retreat. Do not chase beyond the road to Briar Hollow.

encounters.end: The party reaches Briar Hollow or knowingly chooses a suicidal stand.

encounters.objective: Stop the father before he destroys Briar Hollow.
encounters.start: The gaunt, feverish father crashes into Briar Hollow following Torren's scent and the egg. He is operating under Ragged Exhaustion.
encounters.bypass: Throw the party's remaining rations into the square; he eats them and leaves.

creatures.name: Ragged Father Owlbear
creatures.attack: Multiattack: Beak +7 to hit, 1d10+5 piercing; Claws +7 to hit, 2d8+5 slashing.
creatures.trait: Ragged Exhaustion: Disadvantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws. Initiative is made with Disadvantage.
creatures.tactics: Attack anyone blocking the egg or food. Smash structures if ignored.

encounters.end: He leaves after eating the party's rations, dies (revealing unsafe meat and triggering the mother's scream), or destroys the village if ignored.

encounters.objective: Survive the mother's dawn attack after the egg is eaten.
encounters.start: She enters the square already in Maternal Rage.
encounters.bypass: Evacuate rather than defend the village.

creatures.name: Enraged Mother Owlbear
creatures.attack: Multiattack: Beak +8 to hit, 1d10+7 piercing while raging; two Claws +8 to hit, 2d8+7 slashing each while raging.
creatures.trait: Maternal Rage (1/day, 1 minute): Advantage on Strength checks/saves; +2 Strength-melee damage; resistance to all damage except psychic.
creatures.tactics: Prioritize creatures near shell remains, then anyone who damages her.

encounters.end: She is defeated, driven off, or the village is evacuated.

encounters.objective: Resolve the returned-egg consequence based on the father's fate.
encounters.start: The mother retrieves the egg and it hatches. If the father survived, she withdraws with the hatchling. If he died, she recognizes the loss and turns on Briar Hollow.
encounters.bypass: Father alive: no combat; give the family space to leave. Father dead: evacuate the village.

creatures.name: Enraged Mother Owlbear
creatures.attack: Multiattack: Beak +8 to hit, 1d10+7 piercing while raging; two Claws +8 to hit, 2d8+7 slashing each while raging.
creatures.trait: Maternal Rage (1/day, 1 minute): Advantage on Strength checks/saves; +2 Strength-melee damage; resistance to all damage except psychic.
creatures.tactics: Drive straight toward the village defenders while keeping the hatchling behind her.

creatures.name: Owlbear Hatchling
creatures.attack: Beak +4 to hit, 1d6+2 piercing; Claws +4 to hit, 1d8+2 slashing.
creatures.trait: Half-Grown Profile: roughly half a healthy adult owlbear's combat output and durability; imprints behaviorally.
creatures.tactics: Snaps at nearby legs and follows the mother's target; it is not a serious damage source.

encounters.end: Father alive: family withdraws peacefully. Father dead: mother is driven off/defeated, or the village evacuates.

encounters.objective: Resolve whether the party yields the imprinted hatchling or stands between it and its mother.
encounters.start: The hatchling has imprinted when the mother's booming call reaches Briar Hollow. Father alive: she approaches cautiously. Father dead: she arrives hostile.
encounters.bypass: Yield the hatchling and back away. With the father alive, this ends peacefully without a roll.

creatures.name: Enraged Mother Owlbear
creatures.attack: Multiattack: Beak +8 to hit, 1d10+7 piercing while raging; two Claws +8 to hit, 2d8+7 slashing each while raging.
creatures.trait: Maternal Rage (1/day, 1 minute): Advantage on Strength checks/saves; +2 Strength-melee damage; resistance to all damage except psychic.
creatures.tactics: Recover the hatchling first. If father alive, posture before attacking; if father dead, focus on threats associated with his death.

creatures.name: Owlbear Hatchling
creatures.attack: Beak +4 to hit, 1d6+2 piercing; Claws +4 to hit, 1d8+2 slashing.
creatures.trait: Half-Grown Profile: roughly half a healthy adult owlbear's combat output and durability; imprints behaviorally.
creatures.tactics: Avoids serious fighting; moves toward bonded protector unless the mother physically gathers it.

encounters.end: The hatchling remains with the party, reunites with its mother, the party evacuates with it, or the mother confrontation is resolved by combat.

rewards.when: The party feeds its final rations to the father.
rewards.reward: The village survives the attack without killing him, but cannot replace the party's food. They go hungry.
Sella gives the party a standing village favor rather than food the village does not have.
The baby owlbear imprints on a random present PC or named NPC; this is a responsibility/story reward, not a combat pet entitlement.

features: thin communal food table near center
two doomed spear villagers begin adjacent to father

mapNotes.dimensions: Village square at dawn, roughly 60 x 60 ft.
Village edge and field, roughly 80 x 60 ft.
Bakehouse and village lane, roughly 50 x 40 ft. if the mother confrontation becomes tactical.
features: hatchling begins beside its imprinted protector
mother approaches from the ridge-side lane
open square provides a clear surrender path
rear lane allows evacuation with the hatchling

cards.title: Baby Owlbear
cards.front: A damp hatchling with oversized paws, soft brown feathers, huge yellow eyes, and the unsteady balance of something born hungry and dangerous.

back.location: Mara’s Bakehouse at hatching; afterward wherever its bonded PC goes.
dialogue: If separated from its bonded PC: a rising, panicked owl-like trill.
rules: Half-Grown Profile: AC 12, HP 30, Speed 30 ft.; roughly half an adult owlbear's durability/output.
Beak +4, 1d6+2 piercing; Claws +4, 1d8+2 slashing.
Imprint: bonds behaviorally to the PC who most clearly held, fed, protected, or soothed it.
Animal Handling DC 12 calms it for 1 hour.
dmNotes: Use the imprint as the final emotional beat if the egg survives.
Do not let Elmorrow steal the baby off-screen after the players earn this ending.
The baby is a responsibility, not a combat reward.

cards.imageAlt: Newly hatched baby owlbear with oversized paws, soft brown feathers, and bright yellow eyes.

cards.title: Ragged Father Owlbear
cards.front: A gaunt adult owlbear with ribs showing through mud-black feathers, trembling legs, foam at the beak, and eyes that keep snapping toward food.

back.role: Main feed-or-fight encounter; a normal adult owlbear crippled by starvation and exhaustion
back.location: Briar Hollow Square, smashing through the smokehouse toward the food table.
dialogue: No speech. Ragged hoots, wet beak-snaps, and desperate growls whenever food moves.
back.stats: CR 3 base · AC 13 · HP 59 · Speed 40 ft. · Ragged Exhaustion
rules: Multiattack: Beak +7, 1d10+5 piercing; Claws +7, 2d8+5 slashing.
Ragged Exhaustion: Disadvantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws; Initiative also at Disadvantage.
Feverish Hunger: giving the party's pooled one-day rations ends the attack; throwing them from 20 ft. works automatically.
If killed, the carcass is visibly sick and unsafe to eat.
dmNotes: He is starving, not evil. He prioritizes visible food over creatures whenever possible.
If he dies, immediately trigger the mother’s distant scream.
Never turn the sick carcass into a food reward; that undercuts the dilemma.

cards.imageAlt: Gaunt feverish adult male owlbear with ragged feathers, visible ribs, and foam at the beak.

cards.title: Enraged Mother Owlbear
cards.front: A scarred, massive mother owlbear emerging from the ridge mist, shoulders rolling beneath wet feathers as grief hardens into protective rage.

back.role: Overwhelming parental pressure / enraged family consequence
back.location: Ridge woods outside Briar Hollow; may approach only if the egg/hatchling is endangered or returned.
dialogue: No speech. A deep booming scream that sends birds out of the trees.
back.stats: AC 14 · HP 95 · Speed 40 ft. · Maternal Rage
rules: Multiattack: Beak +8; two Claws +8.
Maternal Rage (1/day, 1 minute): Advantage on Strength checks/saves; +2 Strength-melee damage.
Bear-Rage Resistance: resistance to all damage except psychic while raging.
Return/Keep outcomes depend on father's fate; a genuine peaceful reunion remains possible if he survived.
dmNotes: Her behavior follows what the party actually did; never force a fight after a genuine peaceful return.
The keep ending must still account for her; she is searching for her surviving offspring.
If the father died, grief keeps her hostile. Evacuation is always a legal alternative to fighting.

cards.imageAlt: Enormous scarred mother owlbear on a dark forest ridge, nearly twice the father’s bulk.

cards.title: Mayor Sella Vane
cards.front: A lean, sleepless mayor with ink-stained fingers, a bent ration ledger, and the stare of someone counting tomorrow's dead before today's argument is over.

back.location: Village Square, Granary, and final egg debate.
dialogue: “If there were a good answer, we’d have found it before you got here.”
“I don’t need pretty. I need survivable.”
“Tomorrow, we live with what we decided tonight.”
rules: Knows the true ration count: about 2½ days remain.
Investigation DC 12 on the ledger reveals her own household has taken less than its share.
She accepts any deliberate ending, even one she dislikes.
dmNotes: Play her as fair, exhausted, and unsentimental—not cold.
She prevents the crowd from becoming a mob while the party investigates.
Never use her to declare which moral choice is correct.

cards.imageAlt: Exhausted village mayor holding a worn ration ledger in both hands.

cards.title: Mara Dell
cards.front: A flour-dusted baker with oven burns on both forearms, a cleaver resting flat on the table, and hungry children never far from her thoughts.

back.role: Strongest argument for cooking the egg
dialogue: “You can’t feed a village with ideals.”
“One proper meal. Tomorrow we are hungry again.”
“Warm shell or not, I’ve got children chewing bark.”
rules: Knows exactly how far the remaining food can stretch.
Confirms the father’s carcass is unusable if he dies.
Will cook the egg if the final decision goes that way, but will not seize it herself.
dmNotes: Do not portray Mara as cruel. Her position should remain morally defensible.
She openly admits the omelet buys only one communal meal plus broth.
Her strongest scenes are short, practical statements rather than speeches.

cards.imageAlt: Flour-dusted village baker beside a worktable, with a cleaver resting flat rather than raised.

cards.title: Torren Vale
cards.front: A soot-stained hunter with a fresh claw wound across his face, cut rope at his belt, and hands that shake whenever the egg moves.

back.role: Hunter who stole the egg / advocates raising it
back.location: Village Square and final egg debate.
dialogue: “I thought it was food until it moved.”
“I stole it. I know what that makes me.”
“If we crack it now, then all I brought home was another corpse.”
rules: Long fresh scratch across his face came from an adult owlbear during the theft.
Insight DC 10: his 'found it' story is false; he stole the egg from an active nest.
His position is to keep and raise the hatchling.
dmNotes: He is not the red herring anymore; his guilt is real and obvious.
Use him to reveal the theft quickly, not to create another investigation branch.
He should sound shaken rather than heroic.

cards.imageAlt: Soot-stained charcoal burner carrying cut rope, stained blankets, and a hooked woods knife.

cards.title: Elmorrow Reed
cards.front: A clean-bearded man in a moss-green cloak with a polished staff, practiced compassion, and a healer's wagon that smells faintly of bitter sedatives.

back.role: Red-herring 'return it' advocate / hidden circus broker
back.location: Village Square, then his green wagon after the father attack.
dialogue: “The kindest thing is to return it to the wild.”
“Give it to me. I know where creatures like this belong.”
When exposed: “A cage is safer than a grave.”
rules: Nature DC 12: his druid lore is shallow and rehearsed.
Strongbox puzzle: EGG → CHAIN → TENT → COIN.
Wagon evidence proves he works for the Moonpetal Traveling Menagerie.
If exposed, he bargains or flees rather than becoming a boss fight.
dmNotes: He is the misleading 'clean' answer during the first debate.
The fake-druid reveal happens after the father attack, before the true egg choice.
Do not let his lie become a permanent fourth branch.

cards.imageAlt: Moss-cloaked false druid with a polished wooden staff beside a green animal-handler wagon.

flowContract.principle: One linear spine. Branch only when a player choice creates a genuinely different consequence.

clock.name: The Egg Hatches at Dawn

segments.label: Knock
segments.sign: The egg knocks once from inside.

segments.label: Hairline crack
segments.sign: After the father attack, a thin crack appears near the broad end.

segments.label: Spreading crack
segments.sign: During the Elmorrow reveal, the crack branches and the shell rocks.

segments.label: Hatching
segments.sign: At the final choice the shell is warm, moving, and visibly close to breaking.

clock.rule: Advance the fiction clock when the party finishes each core stage. It creates urgency but never deletes a legal ending.
